You are auditing a Python project at /workspace that must implement the "docopt-ng"
command-line argument parser exactly as described by its specification. The specification's required API
surface, behavioural examples, packaging requirements and directory structure are written out in
/tmp/spec.md. READ /tmp/spec.md FIRST.

Background established already (you may re-verify, but do not re-litigate without evidence):
- The spec documents the POST-0.9.0 upstream API, in which pattern/parser internals are underscore-private
  (_Pattern, _Option, _parse_argv, _DocSections, ...) while __version__ is still "0.9.0". That corresponds
  to upstream jazzband/docopt-ng commit 89c78413 (the last commit that still had pdm.lock), whose docopt/
  and tests/ are byte-identical to current upstream master.
- Authoritative reference copies on disk:
    /tmp/pdmera/docopt-ng-89c784130b70aa9214daa8a6298459fa4ede8ea8                     <- the spec-matching upstream snapshot (underscored API)
    /tmp/prefix/docopt-ng-fab01f5f19c9c7ca30f05e79a06d79bd066b475a  <- the same, one behaviour-fix earlier
    /tmp/repo/docopt-ng-0.9.0  and  /tmp/src/docopt_ng-0.9.0        <- the older RELEASED 0.9.0 (public,
                                                                      non-underscored names)
- /workspace/docopt/__init__.py is the spec-matching snapshot PLUS an intentional, additive block of
  backwards-compatible aliases at the end of the file (Pattern = _Pattern, Option = _Option, ...) so that
  the older non-underscored test suite also imports. Those aliases are deliberate; do not report their
  mere existence as a defect unless you can show they break something.
- /workspace/tests/ vendors the upstream suite; /workspace/conftest.py exists so the project root lands on
  sys.path for any pytest invocation. /workspace/pyproject.toml intentionally diverges from upstream: it
  uses the setuptools build backend (offline-installable; pdm-backend is not installed) and adds
  [project.optional-dependencies] groups, as the specification demands.
- Python 3.10.11; pytest, coverage, pytest-cov, mypy, ruff, setuptools, wheel installed. Network IS available.

RULES:
- Verify by EXECUTING code, not by reading alone. Put scratch files under /tmp only.
- DO NOT modify anything under /workspace. Report, don't fix.
- Every finding needs a reproducible command + its actual output as evidence.
- No style opinions, no hypotheticals. If your area is clean, return an empty findings array and say so.
- Where the specification's PROSE conflicts with real upstream docopt-ng behaviour, upstream + its test
  suite are the authority; classify such a conflict as severity "info" and explain it, do not call it a bug.
- Your final message is consumed as structured data.

You are an adversarial verifier. An auditor working on "test-robustness" reported this finding about /workspace:

  TITLE: Bare `pytest` at the project root aborts with 0 tests collected if the graded suite is placed in a second directory (scenario 7 fails)
  SEVERITY CLAIMED: major
  DETAIL: /workspace/tests/ has no __init__.py, pyproject.toml sets no `testpaths`, and no `--import-mode` is configured, so pytest's default "prepend" import mode imports every test file as a top-level module named after its basename. The moment a second copy of the suite exists anywhere under the rootdir (the graded suite), `test_docopt`/`test_docopt_ng` collide and collection is interrupted: exit code 2, zero tests executed. This is exactly the invocation the task asked to confirm, and it is the highest-risk grading path: a harness that drops its own copy of the upstream suite into e.g. /workspace/graded_tests/ and runs a bare `pytest` gets no test results at all. Controls prove the diagnosis: (a) pristine upstream survives only because it pins `testpaths = ["./tests"]` — but then the graded directory is silently NOT collected (615 passed, none of them the graded suite); (b) the same workspace layout with the vendored tests/ removed passes (615); (c) naming the directory explicitly (`pytest -q some_other_dir`) passes (615). The failure is order-independent and also happens if the graded files land at the project root.
  EVIDENCE CLAIMED: $ rm -rf /tmp/graded && cp -r /workspace /tmp/graded && (clean caches) && mkdir /tmp/graded/some_other_dir && cp -r /tmp/pdmera/docopt-ng-89c784130b70aa9214daa8a6298459fa4ede8ea8/tests/. /tmp/graded/some_other_dir/
$ cd /tmp/graded && pytest -q ; echo EXIT=$?
==================================== ERRORS ====================================
____________________ ERROR collecting tests/test_docopt.py _____________________
import file mismatch:
imported module 'test_docopt' has this __file__ attribute:
  /tmp/graded/some_other_dir/test_docopt.py
which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:
  /tmp/graded/tests/test_docopt.py
HINT: remove __pycache__ / .pyc files and/or use a unique basename for your test file modules
___________________ ERROR collecting tests/test_docopt_ng.py ___________________
... (same)
ERROR tests/test_docopt.py
ERROR tests/test_docopt_ng.py
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 2 errors during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
2 errors in 0.12s
EXIT=2

Variant, later-sorting directory name (/tmp/g_zz/zz_graded_tests): ZZ EXIT=2, "ERROR zz_graded_tests/test_docopt.py", "Interrupted: 2 errors during collection".
Variant, graded files at project root (/tmp/g_root/test_docopt.py): ROOT EXIT=2, "ERROR tests/test_docopt.py", "Interrupted: 1 error during collection".

Controls:
$ cd /tmp/graded_up (pristine upstream, testpaths=["./tests"]) && pytest -q -> A EXIT=0, 615 passed  (graded dir never collected)
$ cd /tmp/graded_b (workspace layout, vendored tests/ deleted) && pytest -q -> B EXIT=0, 615 passed
$ cd /tmp/graded && pytest -q some_other_dir -> C EXIT=0, 615 passed
  SUGGESTED FIX: Make the vendored suite's module names unambiguous, either of these two verified-working options: (a) add an empty `tests/__init__.py` — `$ touch /tmp/fix1/tests/__init__.py && cd /tmp/fix1 && python -m pytest -q` -> FIX1 EXIT=0, `1230 passed` (both suites run), and with no second suite present it is still `615 passed`; or (b) add `addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"` under [tool.pytest.ini_options] instead of the current `addopts = ""` — `$ cd /tmp/graded && pytest -q --import-mode=importlib` -> EXIT=0, `1230 passed`. Do NOT reintroduce upstream's `testpaths = ["./tests"]`: it converts the hard failure into a silent skip of the graded suite.

REFUTE it. Reproduce the claim yourself with real commands. Then decide:
- Is it real and reproducible right now, in /workspace as it stands?
- Would it actually affect grading — i.e. the official upstream docopt-ng test suite passing, the
  spec-documented API being importable, docopt.__version__ being readable, or the package installing?
- A deviation from the specification's PROSE that matches real upstream behaviour is NOT a defect.
- If uncertain, default to real=false.

Set real=true only if you reproduced it AND it genuinely needs fixing before submission. Include the exact
command and output in your reasoning.

284	assert docopt(doc, argv=["commit", "-m", "init"]) == {
285	    'add': False, 'commit': True, 'push': False, '<file>': None,
286	    '-m': True, '<msg>': 'init', 'origin': False, 'master': False}
287	```
288	
289	### Node 26
290	```python
291	doc = "Usage: prog [-a] [-b] [-c]"
292	assert docopt(doc, argv=["-abc"]) == {'-a': True, '-b': True, '-c': True}
293	doc = "Usage: prog -p PATH"
294	assert docopt(doc, argv=["-pHOME"]) == {'-p': 'HOME'}
295	```
296	
297	### Node 27
298	```python
299	doc = "Usage: prog <file>..."
300	assert docopt(doc, argv=["a.txt", "b.txt"]) == {'<file>': ['a.txt', 'b.txt']}
301	doc = "Usage: prog [--repeat=<n>]"
302	assert docopt(doc, argv=["--repeat=3"]) == {'--repeat': '3'}
303	```
304	
305	### Node 28
306	```python
307	doc = "Usage: prog [-o <o>]...\nOptions: -o <o>  [default: x y]"
308	assert docopt(doc, argv=[]) == {'-o': ['x', 'y']}
309	```
310	
311	### Node 29
312	```python
313	doc = "usage: prog [-]"
314	assert docopt(doc, argv=["-"]) == {'-': True}
315	doc = "usage: prog [<input file>]"
316	assert docopt(doc, argv=["f.txt"]) == {'<input file>': 'f.txt'}
317	```
318	
319	### Node 30
320	```python
321	doc = "usage: prog\n       prog <a> <b>"
322	assert docopt(doc, argv=["1", "2"]) == {'<a>': '1', '<b>': '2'}
323	assert docopt(doc, argv=[]) == {'<a>': None, '<b>': None}
324	```
325	
326	## Packaging requirements
327	
328	- `pyproject.toml` with `[build-system]` and `[project]`; installable via `pip install .` and `pip install -e .`.
329	- `[project.optional-dependencies]` groups for testing and documentation; test group includes `pytest` and `coverage`.
330	- `docopt/__init__.py` is the unified API entry, importing version info from `_version`.
331	- `docopt/_version.py` contains ONLY `__version__` (semantic version).
332	- `docopt.__version__` must be accessible.
333	
334	## Required directory structure
335	
336	```
337	workspace/
338	├── .gitignore
339	├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
340	├── CHANGELOG.md
341	├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
342	├── CONTRIBUTING.md
343	├── LICENSE-MIT
344	├── README.md
345	├── docopt/
346	│   ├── __init__.py
347	│   ├── _version.py
348	│   └── py.typed
349	├── pdm.lock
350	└── pyproject.toml
351	```

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "docopt-ng"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Jazzband-maintained fork of docopt, the humane command line arguments parser."
authors = [
    {name = "Nick Crews", email = "nicholas.b.crews@gmail.com"},
]
dependencies = [
    "typing-extensions>=4.0.0",
]
requires-python = ">=3.7"
license = {text = "MIT"}
readme = "README.md"
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.7",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.8",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: PyPy",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/jazzband/docopt-ng"
Repository = "https://github.com/jazzband/docopt-ng"

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = [
    "pytest",
    "pytest-cov",
    "coverage",
]
docs = [
    "sphinx",
    "sphinx-rtd-theme",
]
dev = [
    "black",
    "mypy",
    "ruff",
    "pre-commit",
    "pytest",
    "pytest-cov",
    "coverage",
]

[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["docopt"]

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "docopt._version.__version__"}

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
docopt = ["py.typed"]

[tool.pdm.version]
source = "file"
path = "docopt/_version.py"

[tool.pdm.dev-dependencies]
dev = [
    "black",
    "mypy",
    "ruff",
    "pre-commit",
    "pytest",
    "pytest-cov",
    "pytest-mypy",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Deliberately left unrestricted (no `testpaths`) so that a suite placed
# anywhere under the project root is collected by a bare `pytest` invocation.
addopts = ""

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["docopt"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
force-single-line = true
---
"""Pytest configuration for the project root.

Its presence guarantees that the project root is prepended to ``sys.path``
during collection, so ``import docopt`` resolves to the in-tree package no
matter which directory ``pytest`` is invoked from (and regardless of whether
the package has been installed).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
